data.narrative:
Intuitive Machines is a SPAC-stage space and aerospace company that has raised $305M to date. The valuation universe comprises 5 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers including SpaceX and Rocket Lab, though the private set lacks sufficient homogeneity for narrow peer-median analysis—only 2 same-stage comparables exist with no adjacent-stage or similar-tier peers meeting the ≥3 datapoint threshold.

Two standard triangulation methods prove inapplicable here. Peer-median anchoring requires at least 3 comparable datapoints within tightly filtered parameters; the Space & Aerospace sector contains 14 peers total, but applying stage, timing, and valuation-tier filters yields insufficient depth. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples cannot proceed because Intuitive Machines' revenue is not disclosed—typical for private companies at this stage. The median public Space & Aerospace P/S stands at 26.4x across the 5 tickers, but applying this multiple requires known revenue, which is absent from available data.

Without either sufficient private peer clustering or revenue disclosure, traditional quantitative triangulation cannot support a specific valuation range. The analysis indicates that a credible valuation would require either: (1) disclosure of trailing or forward revenue; (2) identification of additional private comparables at equivalent stage and scale; or (3) alternative methodologies such as DCF or venture-return hurdle rates. Current data sufficiency is insufficient for point-estimate or range recommendation.
